item.title: Goroka contractor rebrands PNG DataCo facilities
item.description: Goroka-based contractor Mebiluba Service and Maintenance has commenced refurbishment and rebranding work on PNG DataCo's Kumul Submarine Cable Network landing facility in Alotau, Milne Bay. The six-man team from Eastern Highlands has been engaged to rebrand DataCo facilities across Papua New Guinea to establish a standardized national corporate image.
item.content:encoded:
Goroka-based contractor Mebiluba Service and Maintenance has commenced refurbishment and rebranding work on PNG DataCo's Kumul Submarine Cable Network landing facility in Alotau, Milne Bay.

The six-man team from Eastern Highlands has been engaged to rebrand DataCo facilities across Papua New Guinea to establish a standardized national corporate image.

Director of Mebiluba Service and Maintenance and former DataCo employee Billy Kaupa said the company, which has served as a primary contractor for DataCo since 2022, was tasked with designing and implementing the national rebranding standard.

"It was my idea to design the new branding for PNG DataCo," Kaupa said. "The previous corporate identity used Huawei's color scheme of red, white, and black, but we have transitioned to DataCo's new standard, which incorporates gold."

Kaupa confirmed that Milne Bay is the first province in the Southern region to undergo the face-lift.

"We have completed sites across the Highlands, Momase, and New Guinea Islands regions," Kaupa said. "Alotau is our initial site in the Southern region, after which we will move to Kerema, Daru, Popondetta, and conclude in Port Moresby."

Kaupa said apart from major stations in Madang, Kavieng, and Port Moresby, most DataCo facilities currently lack basic staff amenities.

Following the completion of the rebranding and refurbishment phase, the contractor will revisit each provincial site to install missing facilities, including toilets and showers.

item.title: K1m emergency allocation to fix Matugar Highway seafront
item.description: The Madang Provincial Executive Council [PEC] has approved K1 million in emergency funding to address the severe coastal erosion threatening the Matugar section along the Madang-Bogia Highway. The critical stretch of road has suffered progressive degradation due to rising sea levels and relentless wave action, leaving half the carriageway washed away and posing serious risks to commuters.
item.content:encoded:
The Madang Provincial Executive Council [PEC] has approved K1 million in emergency funding to address the severe coastal erosion threatening the Matugar section along the Madang-Bogia Highway.

The critical stretch of road has suffered progressive degradation due to rising sea levels and relentless wave action, leaving half the carriageway washed away and posing serious risks to commuters.

Madang Governor Ramsey Pariwa confirmed the emergency allocation, emphasizing that part of the highway has already succumbed to shoreline erosion.

"It is now up to the Madang Provincial Administration and the Provincial Procurement Committee to fast-track the procurement process so funds can be released quickly for work to begin on saving the shoreline," Pariwa said.

The seafront underwent temporary remedial maintenance in 2024, but those structures were subsequently washed away, leaving the section exposed to continuous decay.

Pariwa stressed that constructing a durable permanent seawall is essential to secure the road infrastructure long-term.

Given that the affected section forms part of a major national highway, the Governor has also called on the Department of Works and Highways to intervene and provide national support.

item.title: Queensland medical donation to support Lutheran health services in PNG
item.description: A container of medical supplies donated by organisations and volunteers in Queensland, Australia, has been handed over to Lutheran Health Services in Lae. The supplies arrived in Papua New Guinea aboard an Australian Navy vessel and will be distributed to Lutheran hospitals and health facilities in Morobe, Madang and the Highlands.
item.content:encoded:
A container of medical supplies donated by organisations and volunteers in Queensland, Australia, has been handed over to Lutheran Health Services in Lae.

The supplies arrived in Papua New Guinea aboard an Australian Navy vessel and will be distributed to Lutheran hospitals and health facilities in Morobe, Madang and the Highlands.

The donation comes as health facilities continue to deal with shortages of essential medical supplies.

Australian Consul-General in Lae, Brenton Kanowski, said the donation was a practical way of supporting Lutheran Health Services and the communities it serves.

He said the supplies were collected and packed by volunteers in Queensland before being transported to Australia for shipment to Papua New Guinea.

The Australian Government helped facilitate the transportation of the container to Lae aboard the Australian Navy vessel.

Kanowski said the shipment showed how community organisations, volunteers and government could work together to support health services in Papua New Guinea.

The medical supplies include consumables that will be used by Lutheran hospitals and clinics across several provinces.

Lutheran Health Services provides healthcare to communities through a network of hospitals and clinics, including areas where access to government health services can be limited.

A representative of Lutheran Health Services said the supplies would help health workers continue providing care to patients and support facilities dealing with shortages.

The donation was part of wider Australian support delivered during the Australian Navy vessel's visit to Lae.

The vessel also brought two fire trucks and other supplies for community projects.

For Lutheran Health Services, the medical supplies are expected to provide immediate support to health workers and patients relying on church-run health facilities across the country.

item.title: PNG-US disaster exercise builds frontline medical skills
item.description: Papua New Guinean and United States personnel are training in basic emergency medical care as part of a joint disaster response exercise in Lae. The medical training is being held at PNGDF Igam Barracks and focuses on what teams can do in the first few minutes after a person is injured.
item.content:encoded:
Papua New Guinean and United States personnel are training in basic emergency medical care as part of a joint disaster response exercise in Lae.

The medical training is being held at PNGDF Igam Barracks and focuses on what teams can do in the first few minutes after a person is injured.

Participants are learning how to control severe bleeding, manage airways, perform cardiopulmonary resuscitation [CPR], assess patients and prepare them for evacuation.

Medical Planner Major Heather, a US Army nurse with the Wisconsin Army National Guard's 135th Medical Company, said the training began with incident command before moving into CPR and choking response for adults, children and infants.

The participants are now learning the MARCH system, which provides a sequence for dealing with serious injuries.

It covers massive bleeding, airway, respiration, circulation and head injury, while also focusing on preventing heat loss.

The training includes the use of tourniquets and airways. Participants are also being shown how to improvise when standard medical equipment is not available.

Major Heather said the practical sessions have allowed participants to practise the skills and ask questions as they work through different emergency situations.

Patients will be assessed according to the seriousness of their injuries and placed into different priority groups. The teams will then treat the patients and prepare them for evacuation.

The training will form part of the final field exercise, where participants will work with casualties from the search-and-rescue team.

Numiman Trevor, from Engineering Battalion, Bravo Company, is taking part in the medical training for the second time.

The exercise is designed to give participants skills they can use when medical help is not immediately available.

It is also testing how PNG and US personnel work together during an emergency.

The wider disaster response exercise will continue through Friday, when participating agencies will demonstrate how they would coordinate their response to a major disaster.

item.title: Marape: PNG cannot train for the workforce of 1975
item.description: Papua New Guinea must change the way it trains its young people to meet the demands of a modern economy, Prime Minister James Marape says. Marape made the remarks yesterday during the official launching of the new School of Petroleum Engineering at the Papua New Guinea University of Technology in Lae.
item.content:encoded:
Papua New Guinea must change the way it trains its young people to meet the demands of a modern economy, Prime Minister James Marape says.

Marape made the remarks yesterday during the official launching of the new School of Petroleum Engineering at the Papua New Guinea University of Technology in Lae.

He also presented K10 million to Unitch and challenged the university to make sure its training, facilities and courses keep up with changes in technology and industry.

Marape said PNG could not continue preparing students for the workforce that existed when the country gained independence in 1975.

He said the jobs and skills needed today are different, with technology changing the way industries operate.

The Prime Minister said universities must respond to those changes by producing graduates who can compete for jobs in PNG and overseas.

The launch of the School of Petroleum Engineering is one example of the university expanding into specialised areas of training.

The school will provide students with training linked to petroleum engineering and the wider energy sector, which continues to play an important role in PNG's economy.

Marape said the K10 million funding should help Unitech improve its capacity, but he wants the university to clearly set out its priorities.

He has asked the university to provide its infrastructure development plan, saying the government is willing to consider further support if there is a clear plan for growth.

Marape also stressed the need to expand access to higher education for young Papua New Guineans. He said government, universities and industry must work together to make sure the skills taught in classrooms match the needs of employers.

For Unitech, the funding comes as the university expands its training programs and looks to improve its facilities.

Marape said he is prepared to provide further assistance, but expects the university to show how additional investment will improve education and produce graduates with skills relevant to the country's changing economy.

item.title: Funding crunch threatens Queen of Paradise Orchestra’s historic Jayapura tour
item.description: Financial constraints remain a critical hurdle for Vanimo’s Queen of Paradise Orchestra as the young musicians prepare for their maiden international performance in Jayapura, Indonesia, scheduled for the coming weeks. Orchestra program head Fr Martin Prado recently returned from the Indonesian provincial capital after securing concert venues and finalizing preliminary logistics. However, securing
item.content:encoded:
Financial constraints remain a critical hurdle for Vanimo’s Queen of Paradise Orchestra as the young musicians prepare for their maiden international performance in Jayapura, Indonesia, scheduled for the coming weeks.

Orchestra program head Fr Martin Prado recently returned from the Indonesian provincial capital after securing concert venues and finalizing preliminary logistics. However, securing full financial backing remains an urgent priority.

Speaking to NBC News, Fr Martin appealed to the West Sepik provincial government, local district administrations, and national political leaders to step forward and support the youth ensemble.

"We are still looking for funds, hoping that we will receive some help from the district and the province," Fr Martin said.

The planned tour marks the orchestra’s first performance beyond Papua New Guinea’s borders, serving as a platform to showcase local musical talent and foster cross-border cultural ties between West Sepik and neighboring Papua Province.

Fr Martin emphasized that the cross-border engagement offers invaluable international exposure for the young Vanimo musicians, while reinforcing positive youth development through the arts.

In addition to state and provincial support, management is appealing to corporate sponsors and private donors to assist with travel and operational expenses ahead of their departure.

item.title: Permanency plan for Duke of York sea checkpoints
item.description: Permanent sea safety checkpoints will be established following last month’s fatal boating mishap near the Pigeon Islands, according to Duke of York Island local level government [LLG] president Jack Kongkong. The initiative follows the July 18 incident in East New Britain, which prompted local authorities to tighten sea transport regulations between the islands and the mainland.
item.content:encoded:
Permanent sea safety checkpoints will be established following last month’s fatal boating mishap near the Pigeon Islands, according to Duke of York Island local level government [LLG] president Jack Kongkong.

The initiative follows the July 18 incident in East New Britain, which prompted local authorities to tighten sea transport regulations between the islands and the mainland.

Kongkong confirmed four inspection spots are currently operational, including the primary station at the Kokopo beachfront and three peripheral posts at Makada, Kabakon, and Pigeon islands.

The checkpoints are currently manned by LLG officers with assistance from local police and personnel from the Kokopo Police Station.

Kongkong said the disaster was a wake-up call for government action to protect passengers traveling from the Duke of York LLG and neighboring New Ireland Province, noting a history of fatal sea mishaps in the area.

He said the inspection points are designed to enforce safety measures, including mandatory life-jacket usage, strict compliance with loading limits, and preventing alcohol, drug smuggling, and passenger drunkenness on dinghies.

"I will be putting through a proposal at the LLG assembly for these checkpoints to remain for an initial 12-month period, backed by adequate operational funding," Kongkong said. "Once approved, it will be presented to the Kokopo City Authority board for further support."

He said long-term plans include constructing a permanent monitoring facility on Big Pigeon Island.

Kongkong indicated the LLG is reviewing options to raise the passenger limit from six to eight and introduce standardized fares based on route distance. This will be done to address financial losses reported by boat operators due to current travel restrictions,

He also clarified travel restrictions, stating that Mondays remain designated non-travel days to accommodate ward government meetings and community work sessions. Travel to Kokopo on Mondays is restricted unless cleared by a Ward Member a day in advance for emergencies, work, or school returns.

item.title: Prime Minister backs Unitech’s commercial plans
item.description: Prime Minister James Marape has backed development plans for the Papua New Guinea University of Technology [PNG UOT], presenting the institution with a K10 million funding boost during an official campus visit on Tuesday. The funding aims to support sustainable development initiatives across the Lae campus, though Marape cautioned that future financial assistance depends on strict accountability.
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister James Marape has backed development plans for the Papua New Guinea University of Technology [PNG UOT], presenting the institution with a K10 million funding boost during an official campus visit on Tuesday.

The funding aims to support sustainable development initiatives across the Lae campus, though Marape cautioned that future financial assistance depends on strict accountability.

He called on university management to submit outstanding financial acquittals spanning the past seven years to unlock further government support.

Addressing university leadership and staff, Marape urged the institution to maximize the commercial potential of its landholdings, including proposed solar energy projects, while maintaining high standards.

"The government has ministries that only control standards and resource allocation to support you," Marape said. "I am here now to show my support; you have my blessings. Yupla gat bikpla graun i stap, make use lo displa (You have a large expanse of land, utilize it)."

Marape said existing government frameworks such as the Public-Private Partnership [PPP] policy, tax incentives, and operating leases, which the school can leverage to deliver campus projects.

PNG UOT's commercial blueprint includes plans to construct a hotel and shopping centre on campus, alongside formal utility partnerships with Water PNG and PNG Power Limited.

Meanwhile, PNG UoT Vice-Chancellor professor Ora Renagi reiterated the university’s push to acquire the former Telikom College property to facilitate campus expansion, requesting the Prime Minister to expedite an overdue National Executive Council [NEC] decision regarding the asset transfer.

item.title: Western Highlands rejects non-compliance claims, presents reports
item.description: The Western Highlands Provincial Administration has rejected allegations of non-compliance and non-performance, saying it has met its mandatory reporting obligations and continues to deliver services despite limited funding.

item.title: Lawyers warned against obstructing ICAC investigations after SCPNG arrest
item.description: Legal practitioners obstructing the course of justice will face the full force of the law, Independent Commission Against Corruption [ICAC] acting commissioner Don Sawong says.
